To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{3}^{n}{x}^{n+1}}{(n+4)^{2}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{3}^{n+1}{x}^{n+2}}{(n+5)^{2}}\cdot \frac{(n+4)^{2}}{{3}^{n}{x}^{n+1}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{3x(n+4)^{2}}{(n+5)^{2}}| \\  & =3|x|\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(n+4)^{2}}{(n+5)^{2}} \\  & =3|x|\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{(1+\frac{4}{n})}^{2}}{{(1+\frac{5}{n})}^{2}} \\  & =3|x|\cdot 1 \\  & =3|x|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied if 

$$
3|x|<1\,⇒\,|x|<\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\frac{1}{3}.$
